title: Representation-based semantic addressing: can an injected representation reduce routing input without hidden-truth access?
question: Across held-out relations and candidate populations, does representation-based addressing preserve capability while reducing the number of candidates presented to the router?
hypothesis: A representation address index using an encoder trained only from public query/candidate information can retain acceptable candidates at bounded query-time bucket-probe cost, reducing router input relative to exhaustive routing. Exact content addressing remains the control.

arms.name: semantic_address
arms.intervention: use RepresentationAddressIndex with frozen encoder and bounded LSH probes

primary_endpoint.name: success_rate
primary_endpoint.definition: Observed task success using the environment evaluator after routing and execution.

required_controls: exact ContentAddressIndex remains a non-learned control
exhaustive routing remains the capability ceiling
encoder receives only public Query and PersistentState
hidden acceptable_actions and reference_bits are inaccessible to address encoders
no fallback from semantic address miss to exhaustive routing
training data is disjoint from evaluation seeds and held-out relation/population conditions
